paper_claims.claim: The industry-ranked tax-to-book income ratio R_TAX positively predicts subsequent 1-, 3-, and 5-year earnings growth, both before and after the implementation of SFAS No. 109.

The tax-to-book income ratio R_TAX has stronger predictive ability for earnings growth than the deferred-tax-only fundamental R_DEF (the comprehensive tax fundamental dominates the deferred-tax component).
The information in R_TAX about future earnings is incremental to that in cash flows (R_CFO) and other predictors of earnings growth (PRED_1 to PRED_9).

In the post-SFAS No. 109 period, R_TAX is negatively related to the contemporaneous earnings-price ratio, indicating investors price the tax information into current prices; in the pre-SFAS No. 109 period, R_TAX is not priced.

In the pre-SFAS No. 109 period, R_TAX is positively related to subsequent one-year-ahead stock returns (predictive ability not yet impounded in prices); in the post-SFAS No. 109 period, the R_TAX coefficient is small and insignificant.

budget_flag: Tables 2 and 3 alone total ~96 cells (12 G-variants × 8 metrics × 2 panels). The full Tables 4 and 5 are 9-variable E/P and 8-variable returns regressions with mean+t-stat per variable, which would exceed 200 additional cells; we restrict those tables to the headline R_TAX coefficients (mean + t-stat + R² + n), which still exercises the E/P and returns regressions end-to-end.

tables.description: Cross-sectional regressions of future earnings growth on tax and cash flow fundamentals — Eq. (4): G = α_indu + β_1 R_TAX + β_2 R_DEF + β_3 R_CFO + ε, by SFAS-109 subperiod.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of TAX, DEF, and CFO fundamentals from Compustat (current/deferred taxes, accruals components), correct within-industry-year quintile ranking for R_TAX/R_DEF/R_CFO, correct future earnings growth measures G1/G2/G3 (deflated by total assets, percentage points), correct annual cross-sectional regression with two-digit SIC industry fixed effects, and correct time-series averaging of coefficients and t-statistics across years. Downstream claim C1 (R_TAX predicts future earnings growth) and claim C2 (R_TAX dominates R_DEF) both depend on these constructions.
tables.paper_quote: Table 2 presents summary measures from annual cross-sectional regressions of several models nested in Equation (4), with three alternative dependent variables: average annual earnings growth over one (G_1), three (G_2), and five (G_3) years ahead. ... The statistics reported for each set of regressions are the time-series means of the annual estimated coefficients and the associated t-statistics (the ratio of the mean of the cross-sectional coefficients to its standard error). (L1697)
tables.notes: Panel B (post-SFAS 109) Model 1 (R_TAX only) rows G2 and G3 and full-model rows G1/G2/G3 are partially omitted from this commit due to garbled markdown printout of the post-1992 panel; we keep the most-cited cells (Model 1 G1, full-model G3) that anchor the C1 headline. The remaining Panel B cells should be checked against the original PDF (Lev and Nissim 2004, Accounting Review, p. 1060) where the printout is clean.

tables.description: Cross-sectional regressions of future earnings growth on tax and cash flow fundamentals with nine earnings-growth predictors (PRED_1 to PRED_9) added — Eq. (4) augmented.
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates that the R_TAX signal is incremental to nine standard earnings-growth predictors (E/TA, current earnings change, 3- and 5-year average earnings changes, D/TA, R&D/Sales, CapEx/Sales, E/P, B/M) — exercises the full control-vector assembly. Downstream claim C3 (incremental information in R_TAX beyond accruals/cash flows/standard predictors) depends on this construction being correct.
tables.paper_quote: Table 3 presents the results of these regressions (for parsimony, the coefficients of the control variables are omitted). ... our main tax fundamental, R_TAX, is statistically significant in all the configurations of Table 3, while R_DEF is generally insignificant. (L2373)
tables.notes: Table 3 omits the coefficients of the nine control variables (PRED_1 to PRED_9) for parsimony (per footnote 25). We commit the R_TAX-only and full-model (R_TAX + R_DEF + R_CFO) coefficients for G1 and G3 in both panels; G2 cells are structurally identical and are left to the auditor to spot-check.

tables.description: Cross-sectional regressions of E/P* on tax and cash flow fundamentals and control variables — Eq. (5).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of P* (Compustat price × shares × 4-month-post-FYE cumulative return), E/P* in percentage points, and the analyst long-term growth forecast (GROW) merged from I/B/E/S. Downstream claim C4 (R_TAX is priced into E/P in the post-SFAS 109 period only) depends on the E/P regression being correctly specified.
tables.paper_quote: Panel A (Panel B) of Table 4 reports the estimates for the pre- (post-) SFAS No. 109 period. ... in the post-SFAS No. 109 period, however, both coefficients are negative and significant, but the coefficients of R_TAX are larger (in absolute terms) and more significant than those of R_DEF. (L2377)
tables.notes: Table 4 prints 4 nested specifications per panel; we commit the R_TAX coefficient (mean + t-stat) in spec 1 (all 3 fundamentals) and spec 3 (R_TAX alone, controls only), which together span the headline claim C4 (R_TAX priced in post-SFAS, not in pre-SFAS). Control-variable cells are committed only at the level of mean R_TAX coefficients.

tables.description: Cross-sectional regressions of one-year-ahead stock return on tax and cash flow fundamentals and control variables — Eq. (6).
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct construction of the one-year-ahead buy-and-hold return measured from May of year t+1 to April of year t+2 (with CRSP-delisting-reinvestment rule), correct SIZE = log ME at end of April t+1, and correct Fama-French controls (B/P, E/P, BETA, VOL). Downstream claim C5 (R_TAX predicts returns pre-SFAS 109 but not post-SFAS 109) depends on this regression being correctly specified.
tables.paper_quote: Table 5 reports estimates from cross-sectional regressions nested in Equation (6) ... the R_TAX coefficient is positive and significant in the pre-SFAS No. 109 period (Panel A) ... The abnormal return differential between high and low R_TAX firms in Panel A is approximately 5.6 percent (the product of the R_TAX coefficient and the difference between the values of R_TAX for the high and low portfolios, namely 0.014 × [5 − 1]). (L2691)
tables.notes: We commit spec 1 (all 3 fundamentals) and spec 3 (R_TAX alone) for each panel; spec 2 (R_TAX + R_DEF) is structurally a subset of spec 1. The R_TAX coefficient magnitude in Panel A is ~0.013-0.014 with t ~ 3.85-3.91, matching the paper's quoted 0.014 × (5-1) = 5.6% abnormal return differential.
